distractors: The arrival of newcomers into one country, counted at the border and argued about in its politics.
The blending of two cultures into a third that belongs wholly to neither, visible first in the food and in the language.
A community that shares a trade rather than an origin, held together by the work itself and by the annual conference where its members recognise each other and then go home again.

A group that has withdrawn from the society around it on purpose and keeps its own rules inside a boundary it drew itself. What defines it is the choosing, and the boundary is maintained from the inside.

The movement of people out of the countryside and into cities inside one country, which reshapes both ends of it within a generation: labour arrives where the work is and the villages empty out behind it. It is measured by economists more often than it is remembered by families.
